verses.zh: 约伯啊，请听我的话，留心听我一切的言语。
verses.en: “But now, O Job, listen to my words,and hear[NOTE:1] everything I have to say.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “give ear,” the Hiphil denominative verb from “ear.”
Heb “hear all my words.”

verses.zh: 我现在开口，用舌发言。
verses.en: See now, I have opened[NOTE:1] my mouth;my tongue in my mouth has spoken.[NOTE:2]
notes: The perfect verbs in this verse should be classified as perfects of resolve: “I have decided to open…speak.”

H. H. Rowley (Job [NCBC], 210) says, “The self-importance of Elihu is boundless, and he is the master of banality.” He adds that whoever wrote these speeches this way clearly intended to expose the character rather than exalt him.

verses.zh: 我的言语要发明心中所存的正直；我所知道的，我嘴唇要诚实地说出。
verses.en: My words come from the uprightness of my heart,[NOTE:1] and my lips will utter knowledge sincerely.[NOTE:2]
notes: This expression is unusual; R. Gordis (Job, 371) says it can be translated, “the purity of my heart [is reflected] in my words,” but that is far-fetched and awkward. So there have been suggestions for emending יֹשֶׁר (yosher, “uprightness”). Kissane’s makes the most sense if a change is desired: “shall reveal” (an Arabic sense of yasher), although Holscher interpreted “shall affirm” (yasher, with a Syriac sense). Dhorme has “my heart will repeat” (יָשׁוּר, yashur), but this is doubtful. If Kissane’s view is taken, it would say, “my heart will reveal my words.” Some commentators would join “and knowledge” to this colon, and read “words of knowledge”—but that requires even more emendations.
More literally, “and the knowledge of my lips they will speak purely.”

verses.zh: 神的灵造我；全能者的气使我得生。
verses.en: The Spirit of God has made me,and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.[NOTE:1]
notes: Some commentators want to put this verse after v. 6, while others omit the verse entirely. Elihu is claiming here that he is inspired by God.tn The verb תְּחַיֵּנִי (tekhayyeni) is the Piel imperfect of the verb “to live.” It can mean “gives me life,” but it can also mean “quickens me, enlivens me.”

verses.zh: 你若回答我，就站起来，在我面前陈明。
verses.en: Reply to me, if you can;set your arguments[NOTE:1] in order before meand take your stand.
notes: The Hebrew text does not contain the term “arguments,” but this verb has been used already for preparing or arranging a defense.

verses.zh: 我在　神面前与你一样，也是用土造成。
verses.en: Look, I am just like you in relation to God;I too have been molded[NOTE:1] from clay.
notes: The verb means “nipped off,” as a potter breaks off a piece of clay when molding a vessel.

verses.zh: 我不用威严惊吓你，也不用势力重压你。
verses.en: Therefore no fear of me should terrify you,nor should my pressure[NOTE:1] be heavy on you.[NOTE:2]
notes: The noun means “my pressure; my burden” in the light of the verb אָכֲף (ʾakhaf, “to press on; to grip tightly”). In the parallel passages the text used “hand” and “rod” in the hand to terrify. The LXX has “hand” here for this word. But simply changing it to “hand” is ruled out because the verb is masculine.
See Job 9:34 and 13:21.

verses.zh: 你所说的，我听见了，也听见你的言语，说：
verses.en: “Indeed, you have said in my hearing[NOTE:1] (I heard the sound of the words!):
notes: Heb “in my ears.”

verses.zh: 我是清洁无过的，我是无辜的；在我里面也没有罪孽。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] ‘I am pure, without transgression;I am clean[NOTE:2] and have no iniquity.
notes: The word is a hapax legomenon; חַף (khaf) is from חָפַף (khafaf). It is used in New Hebrew in expressions like “to wash” the head. Cognates in Syriac and Akkadian support the meaning “to wash; to clean.”

verses.zh: 神找机会攻击我，以我为仇敌，
verses.en: [NOTE:1] Yet God[NOTE:2] finds occasions[NOTE:3] with me;he regards me as his enemy.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (God) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

The Hebrew means “frustrations” or “oppositions.” The RSV has “displeasure,” NIV “faults,” and NRSV “occasions.” Rashi chose the word found in Judg 14:4—with metathesis—meaning “pretexts” (תֹּאֲנוֹת, toʾanot); this is followed by NAB, NASB.

verses.zh: 把我的脚上了木狗，窥察我一切的道路。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] He puts my feet in shackles;he watches closely all my paths.’
notes: See Job 13:27.

verses.zh: 我要回答你说：你这话无理，因　神比世人更大。
verses.en: Now in this, you are not right—I answer you,[NOTE:1] for God is greater than a human being.[NOTE:2]
notes: The meaning of this verb is “this is my answer to you.”
The LXX has “he that is above men is eternal.” Elihu is saying that God is far above Job’s petty problems.

verses.zh: 你为何与他争论呢？因他的事都不对人解说？
verses.en: Why do you contend against him,that he does not answer all a person’s[NOTE:1] words?
notes: The MT has “all his words.” This must refer to “man” in the previous verse. But many wish to change it to “my words,” since it would be summarizing Job’s complaint to God.

verses.zh: 神说一次、两次，世人却不理会。
verses.en: “For God speaks, the first time in one way,the second time in another, though a person does not perceive[NOTE:1] it.
notes: The Syriac and the Vulgate have “and he does not repeat it,” a reading of the text as it is, according to E. Dhorme (Job, 403). But his argument is based on another root with this meaning—a root which does not exist (see L. Dennefeld, RB 48 [1939]: 175). The verse is saying that God does speak to man.

verses.zh: 人躺在床上沉睡的时候，　神就用梦和夜间的异象，
verses.en: In a dream, a night vision,when deep sleep falls on peopleas they sleep in their beds,

verses.zh: 开通他们的耳朵，将当受的教训印在他们心上，
verses.en: then he gives a revelation[NOTE:1] to peopleand terrifies them with warnings,[NOTE:2]
notes: The idiom is “he uncovers the ear of men.” This expression means “inform” in Ruth 4:4; 1 Sam 20:2, etc. But when God is the subject it means “make a revelation” (see 1 Sam 9:15; 2 Sam 7:27).

Heb “and seals their bonds.” The form of the present translation, “and terrifies them with warnings,” is derived only by emending the text. Aquila, the Vulgate, Syriac, and Targum Job have “their correction” for “their bond,” which is what the KJV used. But the LXX, Aquila, and the Syriac have “terrifies” for the verb. This involves a change in pointing from יָחְתֹּם (yakhtom) to יְחִתֵּם (yekhittem). The LXX has “appearances of fear” instead of “bonds.” The point of the verse seems to be that by terrifying dreams God makes people aware of their ways.

verses.zh: 好叫人不从自己的谋算，不行骄傲的事（原文是将骄傲向人隐藏），
verses.en: to turn a person from his sin,[NOTE:1] and to cover a person’s pride.[NOTE:2]
notes: The MT simply has מַעֲשֶׂה (maʿaseh, “deed”). The LXX has “from his iniquity” which would have been מֵעַוְלָה (meʿavlah). The two letters may have dropped out by haplography. The MT is workable, but would have to mean “[evil] deeds.”

Here too the sense of the MT is difficult to recover. Some translations took it to mean that God hides pride from man. Many commentators changed יְכַסֶּה (yekhasseh, “covers”) to יְכַסֵּחַ (yekhasseakh, “he cuts away”), or יְכַלֶּה (yekhalleh, “he puts an end to”). The various emendations are not all that convincing.

verses.zh: 拦阻人不陷于坑里，不死在刀下。
verses.en: He spares a person’s life from corruption,[NOTE:1] his very life from crossing over[NOTE:2] the river.
notes: A number of interpreters and translations take this as “the pit” (see Job 17:14; cf. NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV).

Here is another difficult line. The verb normally means “to pass through; to pass over,” and so this word would normally mean “from passing through [or over].” The word שֶׁלַח (shelakh) does at times refer to a weapon, but most commentators look for a parallel with “the pit [or corruption].” One suggestion is שְׁאוֹלָה (sheʾolah, “to Sheol”), proposed by Duhm. Dhorme thought it was שַׁלַח (shalakh) and referred to the passageway to the underworld (see M. Tsevat, VT 4 [1954]: 43; and Svi Rin, BZ 7 [1963]: 25). See discussion of options in HALOT 1517-18 s.v. IV שֶׁלַח. The idea of crossing the river of death fits the idea of the passage well, although the reading “to perish by the sword” makes sense and was followed by the NIV.

verses.zh: 人在床上被惩治，骨头中不住地疼痛，
verses.en: Or a person is chastened[NOTE:1] by pain on his bedand with the continual strife of his bones,[NOTE:2]
notes: The MT has the passive form, and so a subject has to be added: “[a man] is chastened.” The LXX has the active form, indicating “[God] chastens,” but the object “a man” has to be added. It is understandable why the LXX thought this was active, within this sequence of verbs; and that is why it is the inferior reading.

The Kethib “the strife of his bones is continual,” whereas the Qere has “the multitude of his bones are firm.” The former is the better reading in this passage. It indicates that the pain is caused by the ongoing strife.

verses.zh: 以致他的口厌弃食物，心厌恶美味。
verses.en: so that his life loathes foodand his soul rejects appetizing fare.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “food of desire.” The word “rejects” is not in the Hebrew text, but is supplied in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 他的肉消瘦，不得再见；先前不见的骨头都凸出来。
verses.en: His flesh wastes away from sight,and his bones, which were not seen, are easily visible.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “are laid bare.” This is the Qere reading; the Kethib means “bare height.” Gordis reverses the word order: “his bones are bare [i.e., crushed] so that they cannot be looked upon.” But the sense of that is not clear.

verses.zh: 他的灵魂临近深坑；他的生命近于灭命的。
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] draws near to the place of corruption,and his life to the messengers of death.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “his soul [נֶפֶשׁ, nefesh, “life”] draws near.”

The MT uses the Hiphil participle, “to those who cause death.” This seems to be a reference to the belief in demons that brought about death, an idea not mentioned in the Bible itself. Thus many proposals have been made for this expression. Hoffmann and Budde divide the word into לְמוֹ מֵתִּים (lemo metim) and simply read “to the dead.” Dhorme adds a couple of letters to get לִמְקוֹם מֵתִּים (limqom metim, “to the place [or abode] of the dead”).

verses.zh: 一千天使中，若有一个作传话的与　神同在，指示人所当行的事，
verses.en: If there is an angel beside him,one mediator[NOTE:1] out of a thousand,to tell a person what constitutes his uprightness,[NOTE:2]
notes: The verse is describing the way God can preserve someone from dying by sending a messenger (translated here as “angel”), who could be human or angelic. This messenger will interpret/mediate God’s will. By “one…out of a thousand” Elihu could have meant either that one of the thousands of messengers at God’s disposal might be sent or that the messenger would be unique (see Eccl 7:28; Job 9:3).

This is a smoother reading. The MT has “to tell to a man his uprightness,” to reveal what is right for him. The LXX translated this word “duty”; the choice is adopted by some commentaries. However, that is too far from the text, which indicates that the angel/messenger is to call the person to uprightness.

verses.zh: 神就给他开恩，说：救赎他免得下坑；我已经得了赎价。
verses.en: and if[NOTE:1] God[NOTE:2] is gracious to him and says,‘Spare[NOTE:3] him from going down to the place of corruption,I have found a ransom for him,’[NOTE:4]
notes: This verse seems to continue the protasis begun in the last verse, with the apodosis coming in the next verse.
Heb “he”; the referent (God) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The verb is either taken as an anomalous form of פָּדַע (padaʿ, “to rescue; to redeem,” or “to exempt him”), or it is emended to some similar word, like פָּרַע (paraʿ, “to let loose,” so Wright).
This verse and v. 28 should be compared with Ps 49:7-9, 15 (8-10, 16 HT) where the same basic vocabulary and concepts are employed.

verses.zh: 他的肉要比孩童的肉更嫩；他就返老还童。
verses.en: then his flesh is restored[NOTE:1] like a youth’s;he returns to the days of his youthful vigor.[NOTE:2]
notes: The word רֻטֲפַשׁ (rutafash) is found nowhere else. One suggestion is that it should be יִרְטַב (yirtav, “to become fresh”), connected to רָטַב (ratav, “to be well watered [or moist]”). It is also possible that it was a combination of רָטַב (ratav, “to be well watered”) and טָפַשׁ (tafash, “to grow fat”). But these are all guesses in the commentaries.
The word describes the period when the man is healthy and vigorous, ripe for what life brings his way.

verses.zh: 他祷告　神，　神就喜悦他，使他欢呼朝见　神的面；　神又看他为义。
verses.en: He entreats God, and God[NOTE:1] delights in him;he sees God’s face[NOTE:2] with rejoicing,and God[NOTE:3] restores to him his righteousness.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (God) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

Heb “his face”; the referent (God) has been specified in the translation for clarity.sn This is usually taken to mean that as a worshiper this individual comes into the presence of the Lord in prayer, and in the sanctuary he sees God’s face, i.e., he sees the evidence of God’s presence.
Heb “he”; the referent (God) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

Many commentators think this line is superfluous and so delete it. The RSV changed the verb to “he recounts,” making the idea that the man publishes the news of his victory or salvation (taking “righteousness” as a metonymy of cause).

verses.zh: 他在人前歌唱说：我犯了罪，颠倒是非，这竟与我无益。
verses.en: That person sings[NOTE:1] to others,[NOTE:2] saying:‘I have sinned and falsified what is right,but I was not punished according to what I deserved.[NOTE:3]
notes: The verb יָשֹׁר (yashor) is unusual. The typical view is to change it to יָשִׁיר (yashir, “he sings”), but that may seem out of harmony with a confession. Dhorme suggests a root שׁוּר (shur, “to repeat”), but this is a doubtful root. J. Reider reads it יָשֵׁיר (yasher) and links it to an Arabic word “confesses” (ZAW 24 [1953]: 275).
Heb “to men.”

The verb שָׁוָה (shavah) has the impersonal meaning here, “it has not been requited to me.” The meaning is that the sinner has not been treated in accordance with his deeds: “I was not punished according to what I deserved.”

verses.zh: 神救赎我的灵魂免入深坑；我的生命也必见光。
verses.en: He redeemed my life[NOTE:1] from going down to the place of corruption,and my life sees the light!’
notes: See note on “him” in v. 24.

verses.zh: 神两次、三次向人行这一切的事，
verses.en: “Indeed, God does all these things,twice, three times, in his dealings[NOTE:1] with a person,
notes: Elihu will repeat these instructions for Job to listen, over and over in painful repetition. See note on the heading to 32:1.

verses.zh: 为要从深坑救回人的灵魂，使他被光照耀，与活人一样。
verses.en: to turn back his life from the place of corruption,that he may be enlightened with the light of life.

verses.zh: 约伯啊，你当侧耳听我的话，不要作声，等我讲说。
verses.en: Pay attention, Job—listen to me;be silent, and I will speak.

verses.zh: 你若有话说，就可以回答我；你只管说，因我愿以你为是。
verses.en: If you have any words,[NOTE:1] reply to me;speak, for I want to justify you.[NOTE:2]
notes: The phrase “in his dealings” is not in the Hebrew text, but has been supplied in the translation for clarification.
Heb “if there are words.”

verses.zh: 若不然，你就听我说；你不要作声，我便将智慧教训你。
verses.en: If not, you listen to me;be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.”
